pr748.title: fix(canonfs): authorize block metadata before side effects
pr748.body:
Block-backed CanonFS publication, revocation and parity-index repair bypass the configured Axion hook on current main. This change invokes the existing hook with the affected reference before any store/index access or mutation, returning `CapabilityError` for denial or callback exceptions. Existing empty-hook bootstrap behavior and read/write semantics are preserved.

Refreshes and replaces #686 without rewriting its evidence. Both changed files are byte-for-byte identical to that PR's head `ac7397aa5f8751d34adcb6ce2d38e3141e65b36c`:

- `fs/block_backed_driver.cpp`: Git blob `3a3b00eb9bc08fcf7ad0a2b866598a3fbf79b4fc`
- `tests/cpp/canonfs_policy_boundary_test.cpp`: Git blob `a9df4a89a86a836df8ed5f92d43ecdc396ba8571`

**Stacked on #747** (`fix/ci-backlog-portability`, parent `122cbec8`), so the policy delta is two files and affected-platform checks include the portability corrections. Merge/review #747 first, then retarget this PR to main. No policy-contract, public API, serialization, capability-enforcement or governance-activation changes.

Fresh local validation (macOS ARM64, AppleClang 21, CMake 4.3, Release/C++23, strict deterministic float ON):

- Applied the refreshed test to the unfixed parent: executable exited **1** at the missing callback-count assertion.
- Applied the driver fix and built `canonfs_policy_boundary_test canonfs_persistent_driver_test canonfs_axion_trace_test`.
- Verified `ctest --show-only=json-v1` contained exactly those three registrations.
- `ctest --test-dir /private/tmp/t81-ci-repair-build-2026-11-09 --output-on-failure -V -R '^(canonfs_policy_boundary_test|canonfs_persistent_driver_test|canonfs_axion_trace_test)$'`: **3/3 pass**. Policy matrix explicitly reports **12 negative cases + 6 positive controls**.
- clang-format dry run, TISC freeze-integrity (209 opcodes), KernelCall ABI freeze (54 ordinals, wire version 1) and `git diff --check`: pass.

Tests retain populated device bytes and read/write/flush counters, check operation/reference delivery, and check no I/O or byte changes before denial. Assertions remain active under NDEBUG. This is fresh execution by the assistant refreshing the implementation, not independent scientific validation.

Limitations: hosted Linux/Windows and other platform results remain required. No full-suite pass is claimed. The capability map remains in-memory, read/write capability enforcement and crash/concurrency/malicious-host guarantees are outside scope. Local build reuses the isolated CI build with local Asio/Google Benchmark source overrides, installed pinned GTest, TUI/examples OFF. Original maintainer checkout remains untouched.

### Parent refresh and validation — 2026-11-10
Current parent is #747 at b18075ad, including the explicitly scoped Windows baseline-document check. The two policy/test blobs remain unchanged. Targeted CanonFS CTests passed 3/3 on the preceding refresh; no policy or runtime code changed in this CI-only parent update. Hosted checks remain required after retargeting to main.

pr747.title: fix(ci): restore supported runners and unblock portability builds
pr747.body:
CI is blocked by retired runners, incomplete Windows build inputs, toolchain errors, and insufficient job time limits. Activating the decoder's Release assertions also exposes a real third-step register overflow.

This repair:
- Moves macOS 14 lanes to macos-15 ARM64 and the macos-13 wheel lane to macos-15-intel; separates CMake cache keys and fallbacks by runner image. [Official retirement notice](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-01-github-actions-macos-14-runner-image-retirement/).
- Includes /development_tests/** in Windows sparse checkout (#641), clears the GDI ERROR macro locally, confines GIC ISB assembly to bare-metal AArch64, and corrects literal/unused-field diagnostics without changing enum values or object layout.
- Builds GTest/GMock with the selected macOS GCC compiler at pinned v1.17.0 commit `52eb8108c5bdec04579160ae17225d66034bd723`. Disables only Google Benchmark's Werror option in AVX2/ASan.
- Makes the existing controlled-AI double-to-float argument conversions explicit for MSVC /WX. Preserves the native 64-bit dimension type in six demo generators, the decoder and its Windows-enabled test; POSIX-only test files are unchanged.
- Gives KernelCallResult string/vector members explicit empty default initializers, preserving their values and layout while resolving clang-cl's missing-designated-field diagnostics.
- Uses <cstring>/std::memcpy in three DPE test helpers in place of the GCC/Clang-only builtin rejected by MSVC. Existing scenarios/checks are preserved; remaining test-file changes satisfy the format gate.
- Removes an unused static tensor-construction wrapper from BM_InferenceComparison.cpp that clang-cl rejects with /WX; all benchmark registrations and exercised calculations are unchanged.
- Includes exactly the five baseline-contract documents required by the Windows sparse checkout. Adds an explicit --docs-only checker mode for Windows because CMake excludes the POSIX integration runners there. This mode labels its result as documentation presence, makes no baseline execution/compliance claim, and cannot combine with --run-tests. Linux/macOS keep the full runner-presence check; the Linux baseline execution step and Windows native CTest suite remain enabled. Frozen contract text is unchanged.
- Replaces all 150 decoder assert predicates with the existing Release-active test helper. With these checks active, the old generator fails on the third greedy step at TWEMBED R244; the VM supports R0–R242. A generated full-vocabulary loop reuses registers while retaining ascending token order and the same row/score operations. Other probe generation is unchanged.
- Raises confirmed Linux GCC/cross-platform job limits from 40 to 60 minutes and the determinism slice from 20 to 30. The sanitizer job's confirmed 30-minute compile timeout is raised to 60 minutes. Decoder/JIT regression tests receive explicit 300/240-second bounds.

Validation on macOS ARM64, AppleClang 21, CMake 4.3:
- Eight checker regression cases pass under normal Python and -O, and the registered CTest passes 1/1. Cases retain default missing-runner/enumeration/execution failure behavior, enforce all five documents in docs-only mode, and reject combining docs-only with execution.
- Actual sparse-checkout before/after reproduction rejects all five missing documents before and passes the explicitly documentation-only check after. The normal full checker also passes against the local configured runner listing; this presence check is not an execution claim.
- Three affected DPE targets build; direct executables pass 20 + 35 + 30 checks (85 total, zero failures). All three also pass x86_64 syntax checks. Functional edits are only the copy function and required headers; unchanged tests are formatted for CI. No native MSVC pass is claimed locally.
- Decoder CTest passes 1/1 in 146.86 seconds with every original predicate preserved; the active-check test failed before the generator correction.
- Controlled-AI authorization/evidence tests pass 2/2; the uninstrumented JIT equivalence executable exits 0 in 79.351 seconds.
- Compiler probes reproduce the old demo dimension-narrowing and HAL missing-field diagnostics; all six corrected demo syntax checks and the complete HAL test translation unit pass with those diagnostic categories treated as errors.
- Six demo generators and the HAL/decoder targets build. All 12 generated model/tokenizer artifacts match their pre-change SHA-256 hashes. The HAL regression executable exits 0 with 3214 checks passed and zero failed; CTest discovers no HAL test in this local configuration, so no HAL CTest pass is claimed.
- benchmark_runner builds after the five-line wrapper deletion. ARM64 and x86_64 compiler checks pass with unused-function diagnostics treated as errors; all 19 registration statements remain identical and 80 inference cases are enumerated without running timings.
- All 25 shared benchmark translation units from the local build configuration pass an AppleClang x86_64 syntax screen with -Werror=unused-function. This uses macOS headers and does not verify Windows-only branches or MSVC.
- 21 workflows parse; 275 Bash steps pass syntax checks; all seven newly changed in-scope test/demo files pass formatting, and git diff --check passes.
- Earlier local checks passed pinned dependency/CLI/hosted-HAL builds, five CanonFS contract tests, tritwise equivalence, sparse-checkout and macro before/after reproductions, and minimal-header cross-target GIC compilation.

[Prior completed CI](https://github.com/t81dev/t81-foundation/actions/runs/42830269177) at `b5178d7c` successfully compiled the complete Windows project with both MSVC and clang-cl. Both jobs then failed the baseline-presence step because sparse checkout lacked five documents; that step also expected POSIX-only runners intentionally excluded by CMake on Windows. The other native lanes and sanitizers passed. These are bounded prior-head results, not verification of current head `b18075ad`. [Fresh CI](https://github.com/t81dev/t81-foundation/actions/runs/42838121136) is queued/running. Earlier cancelled runs are not counted as passes.

Local builds use existing Asio/Benchmark source overrides, installed pinned GTest, benchmarks ON and TUI OFF; examples were enabled for the six-generator before/after check. No full local suite, native Windows execution, release/wheel execution, or new research measurement is claimed. Cross-target GIC checks use a minimal integer header, not an SDK/link/boot test. Baseline workflow audit failures remain: seven tagged action references and qemu-boot-x86.yml's missing permissions declaration.

Draft pending current-head hosted checks and review. Base `e5c30560`; original maintainer checkout untouched. No experiment authorization, research acceptance or governance activation is implied.

pr686.title: fix(canonfs): authorize block-backed metadata mutations (C1-M1)
pr686.body:
Block-backed CanonFS publication, revocation, and index repair currently bypass the configured Axion hook. This change checks the existing hook before each mutation and returns CapabilityError on denial or callback exception. It supplies Publish with the grant target and Revoke/Repair with their affected reference. Read/write calls retain their previous null-reference behavior; an empty hook still explicitly selects bootstrap mode.

Only fs/block_backed_driver.cpp and tests/cpp/canonfs_policy_boundary_test.cpp change. No public API, OpKind, error values, serialized layouts, capability enforcement, or authorization framework changes.

The test uses a populated, byte-retaining IBlockDevice. Across Publish/Revoke/Repair it executes 12 negative cases (explicit denial, throwing callback, missing production policy, invalid production policy) and six positive controls (production allow policy and explicit empty hook). It checks callback count/kind/reference, unchanged bytes and read/write/flush counters on denial, surviving indexed payload/grant reads, successful publication, actual revocation, and repair reads. The checks remain active in Release builds. The private capability map is not directly observable; this does not establish durable capability enforcement.

Validation:
- Before editing, current branch HEAD exactly matched report pin 04f7b30ec4a2171380ead964402147d485be24ec. Comparison with fetched main cda9135d36144d4de2771af174e52ac7b30a83c9 showed no differences in either changed file, Driver header, or CanonStore implementation. This branch starts at that main commit, excluding unrelated local index changes and untracked research reports.
- New regression test built against the unfixed driver: exit 1 at the missing callback-count check.
- Final targeted CTest run: exactly 3 expected registrations verified from --show-only=json-v1; 3 passed, 0 failed. Boundary matrix: 12 negative cases + 6 positive controls passed.
- TISC freeze-integrity: PASS (209 opcodes, bitwise mappings verified, reserved range clean).
- KernelCall ABI freeze: PASS (54 ordinals, wire version 1).
- clang-format --dry-run --Werror and git diff --check: PASS.
- Commit hook bundle validation: PASS.
- Environment: native macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), ARM64; Apple Clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101), CMake 4.3.0, Ninja 1.13.2, Python 3.14.3; Release/C++23, strict deterministic float ON. Linker reports duplicate libt81_core.a warnings; targets build successfully.

Exact configure/build/test commands (paths are retained local scratch):
```sh
cmake -S /private/tmp/t81-c1-m1-source -B /private/tmp/t81-c1-m1-build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DT81_BUILD_TESTS=ON -DT81_BUILD_BENCHMARKS=OFF -DT81_BUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF -DT81_BUILD_TUI=OFF -DT81_ENABLE_TERNARYOS=OFF -DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_ASIO=/Users/t81dev/Code/t81-foundation/build/_deps/asio-src
cmake --build /private/tmp/t81-c1-m1-build --parallel 6 --target canonfs_policy_boundary_test canonfs_persistent_driver_test canonfs_axion_trace_test
ctest --test-dir /private/tmp/t81-c1-m1-build --show-only=json-v1 -R '^(canonfs_policy_boundary_test|canonfs_persistent_driver_test|canonfs_axion_trace_test)$'
ctest --test-dir /private/tmp/t81-c1-m1-build --output-on-failure -V -R '^(canonfs_policy_boundary_test|canonfs_persistent_driver_test|canonfs_axion_trace_test)$'
# From /private/tmp/t81-c1-m1-source:
python3 scripts/ci/check_tisc_freeze_integrity.py
python3 scripts/ci/check_kernelcall_abi_freeze.py
clang-format --dry-run --Werror fs/block_backed_driver.cpp tests/cpp/canonfs_policy_boundary_test.cpp
git diff --check
```

The local Asio override reuses an existing dependency checkout; no unrelated infrastructure was rewritten. No full-suite or hosted-CI pass is asserted. Linux x86_64/ARM64 and Windows x86_64 were not executed: no corresponding native runners were used in this session. Portability acceptance is incomplete; the mock uses standard C++ and the existing IBlockDevice interface.

Remaining limits: externally serialized trusted-owner access and optional bootstrap behavior remain; caps_ is still in-memory and not enforced on reads/writes. Repair still rebuilds an index. Crash atomicity, I/O-failure reporting, multi-process/concurrent revocation, malicious-host protection, and physical side effects are outside this change. No CMP3/H04-R03 changes, benchmarks, SPICE, merges, or activation. Draft for review only.
